description: The Threshold Helipad hangar: a cavernous prefab of corrugated steel, its floor a map of old oil stains and tyre scuffs. Tool racks and a battered workbench line one wall; a wheeled ops desk with a bank of flight monitors faces the other. The big bay doors stand open to the west, framing the ramp and the aircraft parked out on it. Beyond the apron a taxiway peels off and runs dead-straight to a long runway — a broad grey ribbon stretched to the horizon, its dashed centreline dwindling to a pale seam, threshold numbers shimmering in the heat off the tarmac, a lone windsock snapping at the far end. It smells of avgas, hot metal and cold coffee.

flags.intro_lore: Aircraft mean money, and money this far from downtown means somebody worked hard to keep it flying. The Threshold hangar runs on the same principle as everything else out here: whatever still works, works because somebody refuses to let it stop. The runway beyond looks like an invitation. It is, technically — you just have to survive whatever's waiting at the other end of the flight plan.

name: Threshold Helipad Hangar
